content: Human Coronavirus NL63 (HCoV-NL63) is a virus that was first identified in 2003 in the Netherlands in a child suffering from bronchiolitis. Recent studies and reports from various countries, including Australia, Japan, Canada, and Belgium, have confirmed that this virus has achieved global distribution. HCoV-NL63 primarily affects young children, the elderly, and individuals with compromised immune systems, particularly during the winter months when cases of acute respiratory illness are more prevalent. Emerging evidence has suggested a potential link between HCoV-NL63 infection and Kawasaki disease, a systemic vasculitis that occurs in children. Kawasaki disease is a serious condition that can lead to the development of coronary artery aneurysms and is recognized as the leading cause of acquired heart disease in children in developed countries. Further research into the pathogenic mechanisms of HCoV-NL63 is necessary, especially given recent findings that this virus utilizes the same cellular receptor, angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), as the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus (SARS-CoV).
